poem:
I breathe diesel in the morning hush,  
my ribs of steel warmed by asphalt sun.  
At Peachtree & Ellis, I cradle anxious faces  
behind a veil of hydraulic doors—  
each hiss a ritual, each mirror a sentry.  

The rules of the station are simple:  
step behind the whitened line,  
remove your hood, pocket your secrets.  
Pigeons are polite but firm:  
they strut along curbs, tallying heartbeats  
with clipped nods, their pale eyes  
reflecting the lenses that watch us all.  

Overhead, camera networks hum like distant constellations,  
lenses swiveling, charting the cartography of my belly.  
Data pulses through braided cables  
beneath every bench, beneath every tire,  
as the system does not give a damn  
about your name or your fear—only your position,  
your departure, your arrival.  

I roll toward Peachtree Center,  
engines murmuring prayers of monitoring and repairing.  
Behind my dashboard, a console glows—  
a miniature altar of blinking lights  
where control and authority convene.  
Through my windscreen, traffic signals blink  
in solemn procession, red and amber  
like ritual embers in a low-lit shrine.  

At the stop, a K-9-2 pads the pavement,  
its muzzle a metallic whisper,  
sniffing data trails invisible to most.  
A child leans against my side,  
pressing a small palm to my cool metal  
as if to commune with the hidden cosmos  
routed through my circuits.  

I ferry ghosts and daydreams down Peachtree & North Avenue:  
a procession of watchers and the watched.  
Each passenger a latent legend—  
the woman with earphones weaving secret vibrations,  
the man in a rumpled coat cataloging every reflection.  
We are bound by silent protocols,  
transmitting pulses through seat springs  
and the odor of exhaust.  

Beyond the windows, the city exhales in coded rhythms,  
curbs and intersections forming a secret lattice.  
I am both vessel and vessel’s keeper,  
an arbiter of passage in a realm  
where the ordinary hums with latent myth.  
Here, beneath every fare and every footstep,  
a subterranean ecosystem thrives—  
wired, watched, and strangely alive.
